segments.narration: Turf cutters keep digging butter out of Irish bogs. In 2011 two men near Tullamore hit a carved wooden vessel seven feet down.
Inside sat about fifty kilos of pale, waxy bog butter. It still carried a faint dairy smell.
This is not a one-off. Ireland has been burying butter in kegs, churns and barrels since the first century AD. But why bury food?
Bogs are cold, acidic and starved of oxygen, essentially a working fridge. Bristol researchers showed in 2003 that some finds are dairy, others animal fat.
Butter was a luxury in early medieval Ireland, so some stashes were probably hidden from raiders. Others were simply left behind, and never collected.
